newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PM seeks to calm market over finance firms.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM seeks to calm market over finance firms.

text.p: Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh on Monday appealed for calm in the market and told investors that the government would not allow finance firms to suddenly collapse.
"I would like to assure people that the government is closely monitoring and (keeping the) situation under control and there is no cause for concern...," he said.
"The government has handled the BBC (Bangkok Bank of Commerce) case, financial institutions...have been helped with soft loans...Their problems have been eased," he added.

"As to problems of the property sector, we are handling them. As I have said, this government cannot let any sudden collapses (occur). Their problems should be gradually handled. But this does not mean we are encouraging inappropriate business practices," Chavalit said.

"(Any new) government measures being adopted are designed not to create panic but to help calm the market," he said in response to a question about the Thai stock market's halting of trading in bank and finance and securities counters.
The stock exchange said earlier it had halted trading in all bank and finance and securities company shares pending a statement by the central bank and the finance ministry.
